quests.hint: This adjective describes the opposite of explicit - suggested but not directly stated.
quests.explanation: 'Tacit agreement,' 'tacit approval,' and 'tacitly understood' are key. 'Tacit' is very similar to 'implicit' but carries an added nuance of mutual, unspoken understanding.
quests.textToSpeak: There was a ___ understanding among board members that the CEO would resign quietly.
quests.correctAnswer: There was a tacit understanding among board members that the CEO would resign quietly.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is able to be done or achieved within given limits.
quests.explanation: 'Commercially feasible,' 'technically feasible,' and 'not entirely feasible' are key. 'Feasibility' is the noun. More specific than 'possible' - it implies practical achievability.
quests.textToSpeak: The engineers confirmed that the project was technically ___ within the allocated time frame.
quests.correctAnswer: The engineers confirmed that the project was technically feasible within the allocated time frame.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the degree of belief or trust given to a claim or source.
quests.explanation: 'Lend credence to,' 'give credence to,' and 'gain credence' are key. 'Credence' relates to belief and trust, distinct from 'credibility' (a quality a source has) - credence is what you grant it.
quests.textToSpeak: His testimony gave significant ___ to the original account provided by the first witness.
quests.correctAnswer: His testimony gave significant credence to the original account provided by the first witness.

quests.hint: This verb means to make people begin to have doubts about something they had previously accepted.
quests.explanation: 'Call into question,' 'cast doubt on,' and 'question the validity of' are related. 'Call into question' suggests a more serious or systemic challenge to credibility.
quests.textToSpeak: The new findings ___ into question everything the team had assumed about the experiment.
quests.correctAnswer: The new findings called into question everything the team had assumed about the experiment.

quests.hint: This noun refers to doubt or questioning of something previously accepted as reliable.
quests.explanation: 'Throw into doubt,' 'place in doubt,' and 'cast doubt on' are all key. 'Doubt' is fundamental. 'Beyond reasonable doubt' is the legal standard for criminal conviction.
quests.textToSpeak: The conflicting testimonies cast serious ___ on the reliability of the prosecution's case.
quests.correctAnswer: The conflicting testimonies cast serious doubt on the reliability of the prosecution's case.

quests.hint: This verb means to make careful, systematic efforts to find out or prove something.
quests.explanation: 'Ascertain the facts,' 'ascertain whether,' and 'difficult to ascertain' are key. More formal than 'find out' or 'determine.' 'Ascertainable' means able to be found out.
quests.textToSpeak: The committee was unable to ___ whether the decision had been made in good faith.
quests.correctAnswer: The committee was unable to ascertain whether the decision had been made in good faith.

quests.hint: This adjective describes a conclusion or assumption made without adequate justification.
quests.explanation: 'Unwarranted assumption,' 'unwarranted criticism,' and 'entirely unwarranted' are key. 'Warrant' means to justify. 'Warranted' means deserved or justified. Unwarranted is the opposite.
quests.textToSpeak: The harsh criticism directed at the junior researcher was entirely ___ and unprofessional.
quests.correctAnswer: The harsh criticism directed at the junior researcher was entirely unwarranted and unprofessional.

quests.hint: This adjective describes evidence or claims that can be checked and confirmed by an independent party.
quests.explanation: 'Verifiable data,' 'independently verifiable,' and 'not fully verifiable' are key. 'Verify' is the verb. 'Verification' is the noun. 'Third-party verification' means an outside party confirms it.
quests.textToSpeak: The charity published ___ figures showing exactly how donations were spent each year.
quests.correctAnswer: The charity published verifiable figures showing exactly how donations were spent each year.

quests.hint: This adjective describes a theory or explanation that is sound and well-supported.
quests.explanation: 'A cogent argument,' 'cogent evidence,' and 'put forward cogently' are key. 'Cogency' is the noun. A cogent argument is both clear AND well-reasoned. Stronger than 'convincing.'
quests.textToSpeak: The barrister made a ___ case that fully satisfied the court on every point raised.
quests.correctAnswer: The barrister made a cogent case that fully satisfied the court on every point raised.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something absolutely necessary and impossible to avoid or ignore.
quests.explanation: 'Compelling argument,' 'compelling evidence,' and 'a compelling case' are key. 'Compelled' means forced. 'Compelling' suggests the argument is so strong it demands acceptance.
quests.textToSpeak: She made a ___ case for the restructuring that even the most sceptical board members accepted.
quests.correctAnswer: She made a compelling case for the restructuring that even the most sceptical board members accepted.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is basic and essential to the core nature of a thing.
quests.explanation: 'Fundamental flaw,' 'fundamentally different,' and 'fundamental principle' are key. 'Fundamentally' is the adverb. Stronger than 'basic' - it implies foundational importance.
quests.textToSpeak: The study revealed a flaw that was ___ to the theory rather than a product of the methodology.
quests.correctAnswer: The study revealed a flaw that was fundamental to the theory rather than a product of the methodology.

quests.hint: This adjective describes thinking or a method that goes from general principles to specific conclusions.
quests.explanation: 'Deductive reasoning,' 'a deductive approach,' and 'deductive logic' are key. 'Deduce' is the verb. Deductive reasoning starts with a general rule and applies it to a specific case.
quests.textToSpeak: Sherlock Holmes famously uses ___ reasoning to move from clues to a certain conclusion.
quests.correctAnswer: Sherlock Holmes famously uses deductive reasoning to move from clues to a certain conclusion.

quests.hint: This adjective describes reasoning that works from specific observations to general conclusions.
quests.explanation: 'Inductive reasoning,' 'inductive approach,' and 'inductive logic' are key. The opposite of 'deductive.' Science typically uses inductive reasoning - from observed data to general principles.
quests.textToSpeak: The scientist took an ___ approach, building a theory from hundreds of individual case studies.
quests.correctAnswer: The scientist took an inductive approach, building a theory from hundreds of individual case studies.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the process of drawing general conclusions from specific observations.
quests.explanation: 'By abstraction,' 'conceptual abstraction,' and 'abstract the key principles' are key. 'Abstract' is both verb and adjective. 'Level of abstraction' describes how general or specific an idea is.
quests.textToSpeak: The ability to move between concrete examples and higher levels of ___ is a key academic skill.
quests.correctAnswer: The ability to move between concrete examples and higher levels of abstraction is a key academic skill.

quests.hint: This adjective describes an approach or conclusion that applies broadly without exception.
quests.explanation: 'Universal principle,' 'universal agreement,' and 'universal truth' are key. 'Universally' is the adverb. 'Universal' contrasts with 'particular' - applying to all versus applying to one case.
quests.textToSpeak: The philosopher sought ___ principles of justice that would apply across all cultures.
quests.correctAnswer: The philosopher sought universal principles of justice that would apply across all cultures.

quests.hint: This adjective describes an approach that focuses on specific, individual cases rather than general rules.
quests.explanation: 'Particular instance,' 'in this particular case,' and 'a particular form of' are key. 'Particular' contrasts with 'universal' or 'general.' 'Particulars' (plural) means specific details.
quests.textToSpeak: He preferred to deal with each ___ case on its own terms rather than applying rigid rules.
quests.correctAnswer: He preferred to deal with each particular case on its own terms rather than applying rigid rules.

quests.hint: This adjective describes events, phenomena, or qualities that happen together by coincidence.
quests.explanation: 'Merely coincidental,' 'coincidental overlap,' and 'the timing was coincidental' are key. 'Coincidence' is the noun. 'By coincidence' describes an accidental occurrence without causation.
quests.textToSpeak: The similarity between the two documents may be entirely ___ rather than evidence of copying.
quests.correctAnswer: The similarity between the two documents may be entirely coincidental rather than evidence of copying.

quests.hint: This adjective describes something that is deliberately vague or evasive - unclear by design.
quests.explanation: 'Deliberately obfuscatory,' 'obfuscate the issue,' and 'obfuscation' are key. 'Obfuscate' is the verb: 'to obfuscate the facts.' Used when language is used to confuse rather than clarify.
quests.textToSpeak: The contract contained deliberately ___ language designed to confuse rather than inform.
quests.correctAnswer: The contract contained deliberately obfuscatory language designed to confuse rather than inform.

quests.hint: This verb means to express or describe something in a particular way, especially to influence perception.
quests.explanation: 'Frame an argument,' 'frame a question,' and 'how the issue is framed' are key. 'Framing' is crucial in media, politics, and rhetoric. How something is framed shapes how it is understood.
quests.textToSpeak: How you ___ a problem determines which solutions appear most obvious or attractive.
quests.correctAnswer: How you frame a problem determines which solutions appear most obvious or attractive.

quests.hint: This noun refers to the underlying assumptions and values embedded in a text or system.
quests.explanation: 'Ideological framework,' 'challenge the ideology,' and 'ideologically motivated' are key. 'Ideology' shapes political, social, and economic thinking. 'Ideological' is the adjective.
quests.textToSpeak: The report's conclusions are heavily shaped by the ___ of free-market capitalism.
quests.correctAnswer: The report's conclusions are heavily shaped by the ideology of free-market capitalism.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a fixed and oversimplified mental image or assumption about a group.
quests.explanation: 'Challenge a stereotype,' 'reinforce a stereotype,' and 'harmful stereotype' are key. 'Stereotypical' is the adjective. 'Stereotype' can also be a verb: 'to stereotype someone.'
quests.textToSpeak: Advertising has long been criticised for reinforcing damaging ___ about gender and beauty.
quests.correctAnswer: Advertising has long been criticised for reinforcing damaging stereotypes about gender and beauty.

quests.hint: This noun refers to an unfair and unreasonable dislike of or preference for a particular group.
quests.explanation: 'Unconscious bias,' 'confirmation bias,' and 'combat bias' are key. 'Biased' is the adjective. 'Bias' is systematic, while 'prejudice' is often stronger and more personal.
quests.textToSpeak: All research designs must actively minimise the risk of ___ in how data is collected.
quests.correctAnswer: All research designs must actively minimise the risk of bias in how data is collected.

quests.hint: This noun refers to an unfair feeling of dislike toward someone based on group membership.
quests.explanation: 'Racial prejudice,' 'overcome prejudice,' and 'prejudiced against' are key. 'Prejudice' (noun) and 'prejudiced' (adjective) describe pre-formed negative judgements without real basis.
quests.textToSpeak: Awareness alone is not enough to overcome deeply ingrained ___ in institutions.
quests.correctAnswer: Awareness alone is not enough to overcome deeply ingrained prejudice in institutions.

quests.hint: This noun refers to a false or misguided belief about something or someone.
quests.explanation: 'A common misconception,' 'dispel a misconception,' and 'widely held misconception' are key. 'Misconceive' is the verb. 'Misconception' is different from a deliberate lie - it is a genuine error.
quests.textToSpeak: One ___ about language learning is that adults cannot achieve true fluency after childhood.
quests.correctAnswer: One misconception about language learning is that adults cannot achieve true fluency after childhood.

quests.hint: This verb means to spread information widely and quickly to a large audience.
quests.explanation: 'Disseminate findings,' 'disseminate information,' and 'widely disseminated' are key. 'Dissemination' is the noun. More formal than 'share' or 'distribute.' Common in academic and policy contexts.
quests.textToSpeak: The charity works to ___ accurate health information to the most vulnerable communities.
quests.correctAnswer: The charity works to disseminate accurate health information to the most vulnerable communities.

quests.hint: This verb means to officially make something less strict or more relaxed in its application.
quests.explanation: 'Relax restrictions,' 'relax standards,' and 'relax the rules on' are key. 'Relaxation of rules' or 'relaxation of controls' is used in policy contexts. Different from 'relax' (unwind).
quests.textToSpeak: The government plans to ___ planning restrictions to allow more homes to be built.
quests.correctAnswer: The government plans to relax planning restrictions to allow more homes to be built.

quests.hint: This verb means to make a document or procedure officially formal and permanent.
quests.explanation: 'Formalise arrangements,' 'formalise an agreement,' and 'formally formalised' are key. 'Formalisation' is the noun. 'Formalise' moves something from informal practice to official recognition.
quests.textToSpeak: The two universities decided to ___ their collaboration with a signed partnership agreement.
quests.correctAnswer: The two universities decided to formalise their collaboration with a signed partnership agreement.

quests.hint: This verb means to officially hand over power, rights, or territory to another party.
quests.explanation: 'Cede territory,' 'cede control,' and 'unwilling to cede' are key. 'Cession' is the noun. 'Cede' implies a formal, often reluctant transfer of something important.
quests.textToSpeak: The company was forced to ___ control of three divisions as a condition of the merger approval.
quests.correctAnswer: The company was forced to cede control of three divisions as a condition of the merger approval.

quests.hint: This verb means to grant something officially, often a right, status, or privilege.
quests.explanation: 'Confer a degree,' 'confer status upon,' and 'the right conferred by' are key. 'Confer with someone' means to consult. 'Conferral' is the noun. Universities 'confer' degrees at graduation.
quests.textToSpeak: The treaty ___ the right of free movement upon all citizens of the participating nations.
quests.correctAnswer: The treaty conferred the right of free movement upon all citizens of the participating nations.

quests.hint: This verb means to make something necessary or unavoidably required.
quests.explanation: 'Necessitate action,' 'circumstances necessitate,' and 'this necessitates' are key. More formal than 'require' or 'need.' 'Necessity' is the related noun.
quests.textToSpeak: The new safety regulations ___ regular training for all employees working in hazardous environments.
quests.correctAnswer: The new safety regulations necessitate regular training for all employees working in hazardous environments.
